In Islamic culture, it is derived from the Arabic word 'Ziyad' which signifies 'increase' or 'growth' and is a popular name among Muslims. In contrast, in Hindu culture, it is connected to the Hindu Goddess Kali, a deity of creation and destruction, who represents the supreme power of the universe. In Hindu mythology, Kali is believed to have emerged from the forehead of Shiva after his deep meditation and her name symbolizes 'the mother of the universe' or 'the mother of all'.

The Moon, in Hindu mythology, is associated with Kali, who is often depicted as wearing a crescent moon on her forehead.
